blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935 in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

rows: Establishment and governance of the central bank
Regulation and supervision of banking companies
Monetary policy, currency issuance, foreign exchange management
Bank licensing, branch expansion, audit, and liquidation

items: Do not confuse the establishment year (1935) with the nationalisation year (1949).
Hilton Young Commission is also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (1926).
RBI Act 1934 governs central bank functions, whereas Banking Regulation Act 1949 empowers RBI to regulate and license commercial banks.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, following the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (1926).
The central legal framework governing its constitution and central banking functions is the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Initially established as a private shareholders' bank, it was fully nationalized on January 1, 1949.
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provides the primary legal backbone for RBI's regulatory and supervisory powers over commercial banks.
